title: Circuit-breaker heuristics for variant bounce throttling and cross-region sink prevention
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Follow-up to the March 2026 cross-region reroute oscillation incident where a combination of policy mesh propagation delay, stale KV cache, and a missing variant safety check caused repeating failovers and model-variant bounce. This ticket scopes a pragmatic, deployable set of server-side circuit-breaker heuristics and guardrails to: 1) detect rapid fallback cycles per-routing-key, 2) temporarily throttle retries to a failing variant, 3) prefer degraded-but-compatible local variants instead of aggressive cross-region escalations, and 4) add telemetry and canary tests to validate behavior before broad rollout.
timeline: 2026-03-01 03:10Z - Incident triggered: regional policy shard reported elevated fallback rate from variant v1.13 -> v1.6 -> v1.13 loops under capacity churn
2026-03-01 03:25Z - Automated mitigations: global routing circuit limited fanout and disabled aggressive cross-region failover for 12m
2026-03-01 04:00Z - Pager rotation and mitigation: roll-forward of short-lived policy TTL and increase in policy propagation verbosity
2026-03-02 09:00Z - Post-incident review: root-cause hypotheses validated against router traces and KV cache timelines
2026-03-05 14:20Z - Design proposal drafted: local circuit-breaker + dampening + variant-compatibility preference
2026-03-08 10:15Z - Proto telemetry panels created for fallback-rate-by-routing-key and variant-handshake-latency
root_cause: Three contributing issues combined: (A) rapid policy mesh propagation delay led to inconsistent precedence across regions, (B) stale KV cache caused routers to misinterpret variant compatibility metadata, and (C) no per-routing-key dampening or circuit breaker existed — so retries/fallbacks could amplify into cross-region oscillation during capacity flaps.
mitigation_summary: Short-term mitigations included clamping maximum cross-region fanout, increasing policy propagation frequency for affected shards, and temporarily pinning high-traffic customers to conservative variants. This ticket implements medium-term server-side controls that are backward-compatible and minimize false-positives: adaptive circuit-breakers, variant-throttle tables, and route-dampening with TTLs.
action_items: ENG-707777-A1: Implement per-routing-key circuit-breaker that trips when fallback-to-fallback ratio > 0.25 within a rolling 2m window; owner: Miguel Santos; due: 2026-03-10
ENG-707777-A2: Add a soft-throttle table to deprioritize immediate retries to recently-failed variant ids for N seconds (configurable, default 90s); owner: Priya Nair; due: 2026-03-12
ENG-707777-A3: Prefer local-compatible degraded variants over cross-region escalation when latency delta < 80ms and quality-delta < configured threshold; owner: Danilo Perez; due: 2026-03-15

ENG-707777-A4: Extend routing telemetry: per-routing-key fallback-count, consecutive-fallbacks, variant-handshake-latency histogram, and policy-staleness gauge; owner: Leah Ito; due: 2026-03-08 (dashboards live)
ENG-707777-A5: Create a static safety check in policy application that rejects a fallback plan if variant compatibility metadata is missing or stale; owner: Miguel Santos; due: 2026-03-11
ENG-707777-A6: Add e2e chaos test that simulates policy-propagation delay + transient capacity loss to validate circuit-breaker behavior; owner: Soren Valdez; due: 2026-03-20
ENG-707777-A7: Update runbook and incident playbook with new detection thresholds and manual override steps; owner: Nora Blake; due: 2026-03-13
ENG-707777-A8: Canary rollout across 10% of traffic with observability gates (fallback-rate, customer-impacted-requests); owner: Miguel Santos with SRE; due: 2026-03-18
acceptance_criteria: Circuit-breaker trips and prevents repeated fallback loops in synthetic replay of the March incident
Dashboards show per-routing-key fallback reduction >= 85% in canary compared to baseline within 30 minutes
No regression in P50 latency for healthy workloads (>99% traffic) after soft-throttle enabled
Runbook updated and on-call has performed at least one simulated mitigation flow
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy feature-flagged implementation to staging and run targeted replay of incident traces
2) Enable telemetry and alerting (two new alerts: fallback-loop-detection, variant-throttle-saturation)
3) Canary 10% traffic for 12h with manual guardrail checks, then 50% for 6h if stable
4) Gradual rollout to 100% with automated rollback if fallback-loop-detection fires in >3 routing-keys within 1h
